Thanks for the notes and attachments. A couple more specifics from our end before the deep-dive: 

- Short-lived tokens: we want to issue tokens that expire in under an hour for inference calls. Is there built-in support for OAuth token exchange or do you expect us to use the SDK and rotate API keys ourselves?
- Key rotation audit: when a key is rotated, do you provide an audit trail showing which key was used for which request (token binding / key id on logs)? Retention for logs is another ask - we currently need 12 months.
- Embeddings / rerankers: for scale we plan to batch embeddings and use a reranker on the topN results. Any impact of auth patterns on batching (e.g., short-lived tokens causing reconnects)?

If you could have engineering address these prior to the call that would help focus the deep-dive.

Hi Alex / Priya -

Thanks for the follow-ups. Quick technical answers and recommended patterns from Redwood engineering: 

1) Short-lived tokens / OIDC / JWTs
- Redwood supports multiple auth flows: static API keys (server-to-server), OAuth2 token exchange / JWTs (recommended for short-lived tokens), and service-account signed JWTs for machine-to-machine auth.
- For your requirement (tokens < 1 hour) we recommend using service accounts + short-lived JWTs minted by your identity provider (OIDC) or via Redwood's token exchange endpoint. The common pattern is: your infra mints a short-lived JWT -> exchange for a Redwood access token (1h) -> use the access token for inference calls. 
- We support the OAuth2 token exchange spec (RFC 8693) and can accept tokens issued by your IdP if you register the IdP in our control plane.

2) Key rotation & KMS integration
- You can store signing keys in your KMS (Google KMS) and have your service account sign tokens; Redwood validates tokens by the public key. For API-key-style credentials we also support rotating keys via our control plane API and tagging keys with metadata (purpose, owner, rotation_date).
- Audit/logging: every request includes a key_id/auth method in the audit logs. Logs include token key id (kid header) and can be exported to your SIEM or to our audit log storage. Retention is configurable - we can keep 12 months for enterprise customers; we also support pushing logs to your cloud logging bucket for long-term retention.

3) Role-based service accounts
- Yes - you can create multiple service accounts with granular permissions (ingest-only, inference-only, admin). Each service account gets its own client_id / credentials and audit trail.

4) Impact on batching / embeddings / reranker
- Short-lived tokens do not affect in-process batching. Redwood's serving runtime batches requests on the server side; the only consideration is long-lived HTTP connections vs. per-call auth. We recommend keeping a short-lived access token in your request pool and refreshing it via token-exchange on expiry; typical pattern is a background refresher that updates the bearer token used by pooled worker threads.
- For embeddings at high throughput we recommend using service accounts with a refreshable token and a small token TTL (30-60m) and refresh logic in your SDK client. That avoids reconnects on every request.

5) Example flow (high level)
- Step 1: PaymentsCo creates service accounts in Redwood control plane -> register your IdP (or use Redwood token-exchange).
- Step 2: Your infra mints short-lived JWTs (signed by Google KMS) -> exchange for Redwood access token (1h).
- Step 3: SDK uses Redwood access token in Authorization header for inference and embedding calls.

6) Sample headers we include in logs: request_id, timestamp, model, route, key_id/kid, service_account_id.

I'll attach a short guide we use for customers implementing service accounts and rotation. Happy to add code snippets for your SDK language if you tell us which one you want (Go/Java/Python/Node).

Attachment: service-account-guide.md

Regards,
